sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 23.09.2022 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pavagada (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.982/2019.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pavagada
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellants seek enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
On 18.01.2019 at about 10.00 p.m., one Adiveppa was proceeding along with one Maruthi, as a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 64-R-2523.

When they reached near Pavagada- Kalyanadurga road, Pavagada, the rider i.e.
Maruthi of the said motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and due to the front wheel of the said motor cycle got punctured, the said Adiveppa, who is a pillion rider fell NC: 2024:KHC:6647 down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Pavagada Government Hospital, wherein he succumbed to the injuries.
The claimants spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and other obsequies ceremonies etc. 3.1
It is stated by the claimants that prior to the occurrence of accident, deceased Adiveppa was hale and healthy, aged about 55 years.
He was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month by doing coolie work.
The claimants were solely dependent on the earnings of the deceased for the maintenance and livelihood.
Hence, the claimants filed the claim petition seeking compensation.

3.2 On service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel, but Respondent No.2- Insurance Company filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

3.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant No.2 got examined himself as PW.1, later claimant No.2 died and claimant No.1 got examined himself as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P13.

On the other hand, respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW.1 and another witness as RW.2 and got marked document as Ex.R1.
3.5

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.9,68,060/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation and also held respondent No.2-Insurance Company to pay the entire compensation amount and thereafter, respondent No.2- Insurance Company shall recover the same from respondent No.1.
Anjanamma @ Anjinamma vs S Maruthi on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137724582/
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellants-claimants that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meagre compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.
Hence, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for appellants-claimants and learned counsel for Insurance Company,
perused the impugned judgment and award, the documents produced at Exs.P1 to P24, the Police records and medical records, out of which the Police records clearly depict the filing of NC:
2024:KHC:6647 FIR and laying of charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle and same has not been challenged or controverted.
Therefore, the tribunal rightly attributed the negligence against the rider of the motor cycle.
The medical records, which clearly depicts the injury sustained by the claimant in the occurrence of accident.

7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month,
as no proof of income was produced.
However, the Legal Service Authority chart prescribes the notional income of Rs.14,000/- per month for the accident of the year 2019 and the same is taken in the present case.
The tribunal rightly taken 10% towards future prospects, which does not call for interference.
The tribunal has deducted  towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
However, it ought to have taken 1/3rd, as the deceased was a married person.
The age of the deceased was 55 years as on the date of NC: 2024:KHC:6647 occurrence of accident.
The appropriate multiplier would be '11', which is rightly applied by the tribunal and the same does not call for interference.

Therefore, the claimants would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.13,55,244/- (Rs.14,000/- + 10% = Rs.15,400/- - 1/3rd = Rs.10,267/- x 12 x 11) towards loss of dependency as against Rs.7,98,060/- awarded by the tribunal.
8. The tribunal awarded Rs.40,000/- towards spouse consortium, Rs.1,00,000/- towards love and affection, Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
However, I do not find any reason to interfere with these heads, as it is just and reasonable compensation.
9. In view of the above, the claimants would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.15,25,244/- as against Rs.9,68,060/- as mentioned in the table below:
